title: Knowledge check: Quality Gates and Continuous Integration

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Quality Gates and Continuous Integration”?
options: Test observable behavior with deterministic setup, realistic interaction, and both a normal case and a relevant failure or boundary case.
Test only private implementation details and ignore user-visible behavior.
Rely on one screenshot as proof of every application state.
Make end-to-end tests the only test level.
questions.answer_key: Test observable behavior with deterministic setup, realistic interaction, and both a normal case and a relevant failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Quality Gates and Continuous Integration directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Running tests automatically”, which practice is most reliable?
options: A screenshot alone proves all component states are correct.
Mock every function even when a real unit test is clearer.
End-to-end tests should be the only test type.
Choose tests around observable behavior and cover normal plus edge or failure cases.
questions.answer_key: Choose tests around observable behavior and cover normal plus edge or failure cases.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Running tests automatically”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Quality Gates and Continuous Integration” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
